text: Which of the following best defines the term "internet" (with a lowercase 'i')?
info: internet (lowercase 'i') = interconnected subnets; Internet (capital 'I') = the global public network.

answers.text: A network of devices strictly inside a computer laboratory
An interconnection of two or more individual networks
A group of computers and printers connected to the same switch

text: Which major historical event occurred in the year 1969?
info: 1969 = Birth of ARPANET connecting 4 original nodes (UCLA, UCSB, Stanford, and Utah).

answers.text: The initial development of the TCP/IP protocol suite
The establishment of ARPANET with 4 nodes
The official declaration of TCP/IP as a standard

text: In 1972, which device was invented to connect networks with different packet sizes and transmission rates?
info: 1972 = Invention of the Gateway to bridge heterogeneous networks.

text: In 1977, internet communication was tested using three transmission media. Which of the following was EXCEPTED?
info: 1977 3-network test = Wired (ARPANET) + Radio + Satellite.

text: Which significant event took place in 1983?
info: 1983 = TCP/IP became standard + MILNET (military) separated from ARPANET.

answers.text: TCP/IP became the official standard protocol, and MILNET split from ARPANET
NSFNET was created using T1 lines
UC Berkeley integrated TCP/IP into UNIX
Private ISPs were allowed to offer commercial Internet services

text: Which backbone network was established in 1986, connecting 5 supercomputer centers?
info: 1986 = NSFNET built a backbone running at T1 speed (1.544 Mbps).

text: In which year was ARPANET officially decommissioned and replaced by NSFNET?
info: 1990 = ARPANET retired and replaced by NSFNET.

text: What major milestone occurred in the internet domain in 1995?
info: 1995 = The start of the commercial Internet era led by private ISPs.

answers.text: IPv6 was used for the first time
Private ISPs began providing commercial Internet services
The Domain Name System (DNS) was invented

text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three key elements of a protocol?
info: 3 Protocol Elements: Syntax - Semantics - Timing.

text: "The element that defines the structure or format of the data, such as indicating that the first 8 bits represent the address." Which element does this describe?
info: Syntax = Data Structure & Format.

text: "The element that specifies the meaning of bits and the actions to be taken upon receiving data." Which element does this describe?
info: Semantics = Meaning & Action.

text: Which key question is controlled by the "Timing" element?
info: Timing = When & How fast.

answers.text: Whether data is correct and who it is addressed to
How data is encrypted and who receives it
When data should be sent and how fast it can be transmitted
How many bytes data contains and which port it uses

text: How does a "De facto" standard differ from a "De jure" standard?
info: De facto = By fact (popular usage), De jure = By law/official body.

answers.text: De facto is approved by law, while De jure originates from popularity
De facto is widely used without formal approval, whereas De jure is certified by an official standards body
De facto applies only to hardware, whereas De jure applies to software
There is no difference between the two

text: Which organization developed and defined the OSI Reference Model (7 Layers)?
info: ISO = Creator of the OSI Model (ISO/OSI).

text: Which organization defines network standards such as Ethernet (802.3) and Wi-Fi (802.11)?
info: IEEE = Handles the 802 family standards (802.3 Ethernet, 802.11 Wi-Fi).

text: What is the primary focus of the ITU-T organization?
info: ITU-T (Telecommunication) = Focuses on telecom and voice systems.

answers.text: Enforcing radio frequency regulations in the US

text: "Wi-Fi Alliance" and "ATM Forum" fall under which group of standards organizations?
info: Forum = Alliances of manufacturers working together to promote specific technologies.

text: Under which category is the FCC (Federal Communications Commission) of the United States classified?
info: FCC = Government regulatory body overseeing communications.

text: What is the official document series used to publish and develop Internet standards called?
info: Internet standards are discussed and standardized through RFC documents.

text: Before a technical specification is published as an RFC, what status does it start with?
info: First stage = Internet Draft -> RFC.

text: What condition must an RFC meet to progress from "Proposed Standard" to "Draft Standard"?
info: Draft Standard = Minimum 2 independent & interoperable implementations.

answers.text: It must have been used for at least 5 years
It must have at least two successful, independent, and interoperable implementations
It must receive a public vote
It must be approved by the US government

text: An RFC document that has been retired because it became obsolete or was replaced by a newer standard is assigned which Maturity Level?
info: Historic = Outdated / replaced by newer specs.

text: An RFC containing historical context, tutorials, or vendor information falls under which category?
info: Informational = General info / tutorials / external vendor notes.

text: Which of the following protocol pairs is classified as "Required" (mandatory for an Internet system)?
info: Required core protocols = IP & ICMP.

text: Under which Requirement Level are FTP and TELNET classified according to the standard internet architecture?
info: Recommended protocols include FTP and TELNET.

text: RFCs with an "Experimental" maturity level are usually mapped to which Requirement Level?
info: Experimental RFCs = Limited Use (restricted adoption).

text: Which body occupies the highest level in the Internet Management & Administrative structure (Figure 1-4)?
info: ISOC sits at the top of the internet organization hierarchy.

text: Which organization serves as the technical advisor and oversees the overall TCP/IP protocol architecture?
info: IAB = Oversees Internet Architecture.

text: What is the main difference between IRTF and IETF?
info: IRTF = Research (long-term), IETF = Engineering/RFCs (short-term & active standards).

answers.text: IRTF focuses on current problems, while IETF focuses on future research
IRTF focuses on long-term research, whereas IETF handles short-term engineering and standards
IRTF manages Domain Names, while IETF manages IP Addresses
IRTF is a private organization, while IETF is a government agency

text: Which management body within the IETF is responsible for administering and approving standards?
info: IETF is managed by IESG (just as IRTF is managed by IRSG).
